citations.quote: A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$.
Then $\mathcal H_c$ is compact and sequentially compact in $\tau_L$.

Let $d\geq1$, let $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, with this class defined in [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], be ergodic under the full translation group $\mathbb R^d$, and suppose its specific relative entropy $I(P)=\gamma$ relative to the unit-intensity Poisson law $Q$ is finite.

Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space and use $D(P\Vert Q)$ as defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(P(\phi)-\log Q(e^\phi)\right),$$
where $B_b$ is the set of bounded real measurable functions. In particular $D\geq0$. If $T$ is measurable, then $D(P\circ T^{-1}\Vert Q\circ T^{-1})\leq D(P\Vert Q)$.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$
More generally, for random variables $R,S,Y$ taking values in standard-Borel spaces $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal Y$, with $R=r(S)$ for a measurable $r:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$, and a probability reference $Q_Y$ on $\mathcal Y$, the conditional increments
$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$
satisfy $0\leq G(R)\leq G(S)$ whenever $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)<\infty$.

For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$.
Equivalently, a net $(P_\alpha)$ converges to $P$ in $\tau_L$ exactly when $E_{P_\alpha}f\to E_Pf$ for every measurable local $f$ with at most linear growth in the count of a bounded support.

For pairwise disjoint bounded Borel sets $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, the restrictions $\omega|_{A_1},\ldots,\omega|_{A_r}$ are independent, each count $N_{A_j}$ has Poisson law with mean $\lambda|A_j|$, and the joint law of counts on any finite disjoint family is the product of those Poisson laws.

Let $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$ be measurable and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$
for every $x$.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as in [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]. Let $L\to\infty$ and let $C_L$ be probability laws on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, invariant under every translation modulo $L\mathbb Z^d$. Write $Q_L$ for unit-intensity Poisson measure and suppose
$$c_L=L^{-d}D(C_L\Vert Q_L),\qquad \sup_L c_L<\infty.$$
Let $\widetilde C_L$ be the law of the periodic continuation. Then $\widetilde C_L=E_{C_L}R_{L,\omega}$; these laws are stationary and are relatively sequentially compact in $\tau_L$ as $L\to\infty$. Their local counts are uniformly integrable. Along any convergent subsequence with limit $P$,
$$I(P)\leq\liminf_L c_L.$$
If the empirical fields $R_{L,\omega}$ converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to a fixed $P_*$, then $\widetilde C_L\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$, including expectations of every measurable local $f$ with $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ for bounded $A$. This concerns periodic continuation, not the zero extension of a configuration outside its fundamental cube.

derivations.claim: Regularity bounds $\phi$ above outside a bounded set, so $B$ is bounded. Define $\chi=+\infty$ on $B$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then $\chi$ is even, stable with constant $0$, and has zero far tail. Its finite-volume beta-zero partition is exactly the specified hard-admissibility partition.

For each bounded region $A$, the event that $A$ contains a forbidden pair is a bounded measurable local event. Its probability is continuous under $\tau_L$ by [F6]. Exhausting space by countably many bounded cubes shows that $\mathcal K_B$ is $\tau_L$-closed. Apply [F4] to the bounded tests $f_M=a\min(N_C,M)$ and let $M\to\infty$. Monotone convergence and [F7] give $I(P)\geq a\rho(P)-(e^a-1)$, hence $\rho(P)\leq(I(P)+e^a-1)/a$. Choosing $a>2\max(\log z,0)$ makes $I(P)-\rho(P)\log z$ coercive in $I(P)$. By [F2], every finite sublevel is compact and lower semicontinuous, so the infimum on $\mathcal K_B$ is attained whenever the admissible class is nonempty. The empty configuration law gives a finite candidate.

Fix $P\in\mathcal K_B$ with $I(P)<\infty$. Condition its restriction to a cube of side $n$ on configurations whose distinct points have separation at least $1/q$ and whose finite pair energies are at most $q$. As $q\to\infty$, these events increase to probability one because configurations are locally finite, simple, and hard-admissible. Choose $q=q(n)$ so the conditioning probability tends to one. Tile space by these conditioned blocks separated by an empty corridor wider than the range of $B$ and the fixed tail cutoff, take independent copies, then average the lattice phase uniformly. No cross-block pair is forbidden. The conditional entropy inequality $$ D(P(\cdot\mid E)\Vert Q)\leq [D(P\Vert Q)+1]/P(E)-\log P(E) $$ follows by expanding the conditional density $1_E(dP/dQ)/P(E)$ and using $-u\log u\leq1/e$. Additivity on independent blocks and the vanishing corridor fraction give $\limsup I(P_n)\leq I(P)$; local count truncation and finite first moments give $P_n\to P$ in $\tau_L$. Each $P_n$ has finite original energy density.

For a finite-volume beta-zero Gibbs law $G_L^b$, direct integration of its density gives $$ -\log Z_{Q,L}=D(G_L^b\Vert Q_L)-(\log z)E_{G_L^b}N_L. $$ Stationarize independent blocks and average their phase. The entropy chain rule bounds the resulting specific entropy by the displayed finite-volume entropy per volume; hard admissibility passes to every local limit. Compactness [F2], lower semicontinuity, and the entropy identity therefore give the pressure upper bound by the negative minimum in the statement. For the reverse bound, use the approximating finite-energy laws from step 1.3. Their independent separated blocks are admissible; the spatial likelihood theorem [F3] supplies typical blocks with likelihood cost $I(P_n)$, while empirical counts converge to $\rho(P_n)$. Changing from Poisson measure to the beta-zero weight gives the lower rate $-I(P_n)+\rho(P_n)\log z$. Let $n\to\infty$ and optimize over $P$. Corridors change the normalized log weight by their vanishing volume fraction, so free and periodic rates agree.

Put $\alpha=\log z$, $p_L=L^{-d}\log Z_{Q,L}$, and $d_L=L^{-d}D(G_L^{\rm per}\Vert Q_L)$. The exact identity in step 2.1 reads $d_L=\alpha\rho_L-p_L$. For $a>\max(\alpha,0)$, the entropy count inequality gives $d_L\geq a\rho_L-(e^a-1)$; the convergent pressure rates therefore bound both $\rho_L$ and $d_L$. The grand density and periodic hard-admissibility condition are invariant under translations modulo the box, so [F8] gives relatively compact continued laws. Every limit $P$ lies in $\mathcal K_B$ by the bounded local forbidden-pair tests from step 1.2. Along a subsequence realizing the entropy liminf, [F8] and count-tail uniformity give
$$I(P)-\alpha\rho(P)\leq\liminf(d_L-\alpha\rho_L)=-\lim p_L=\min_{\mathcal K_B}(I-\alpha\rho).$$
The opposite inequality is the definition of the minimum. Thus every accumulation point is a minimizer. If there is just one, relative compactness forces convergence of the entire sequence in $\tau_L$, including every stated tame test.

Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and let $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. For a finite configuration $\omega$, call it admissible when no pair displacement belongs to $B$; for periodic boxes require this also for every periodic image pair. Define the zero-inverse-temperature-parameter continuation (the mathematical $\beta=0$ branch) to be $z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\rm admissible}(\omega)$, explicitly retaining the hard exclusion. Then the normalized Poisson free and periodic partition rates exist and equal
$$-\min_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},$$
where $\mathcal K_B$ is the set of stationary laws with no forbidden pair almost surely. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in $\tau_L$. The periodically continued grand laws are relatively compact in $\tau_L$, all their accumulation points are minimizers, and if this minimizer is unique they converge to it for every measurable local observable of at-most-linear count growth. If $B=\varnothing$, this is the Poisson activity-$z$ model. For $B\ne\varnothing$, it is not an unrestricted Poisson law and does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and let $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. For a finite configuration $\omega$, call it admissible when no pair displacement belongs to $B$; for periodic boxes require this also for every periodic image pair. Define the zero-inverse-temperature-parameter continuation (the mathematical $\beta=0$ branch) to be $z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\rm admissible}(\omega)$, explicitly retaining the hard exclusion. Then the normalized Poisson free and periodic partition rates exist and equal
$$-\min_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},$$
where $\mathcal K_B$ is the set of stationary laws with no forbidden pair almost surely. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in $\tau_L$. The periodically continued grand laws are relatively compact in $\tau_L$, all their accumulation points are minimizers, and if this minimizer is unique they converge to it for every measurable local observable of at-most-linear count growth. If $B=\varnothing$, this is the Poisson activity-$z$ model. For $B\ne\varnothing$, it is not an unrestricted Poisson law and does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

Fix a positive integer $d$ and use the Euclidean space $\mathbb R^d$ with norm
$\|x\|_2=\sqrt{\langle x,x\rangle}$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. A
pair potential is an even Borel-measurable function
$\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ whose image is contained in
$\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$. Here $\overline{\mathbb R}$ is the extended real
line ([[def-extended-reals]]). Borel measurability means the inverse image of
each Borel subset of $\overline{\mathbb R}$ belongs to the Borel sigma-algebra
generated by open sets in the Euclidean topology on $\mathbb R^d$
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra-on-the-extended-real-line]],
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. The value
$+\infty$ represents a forbidden pair separation. Coordinates and
potential values are numerical values in fixed reference length and energy
units.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $d\ge1$, let $\phi$ be a stable pair
potential as in [[def-tdmath-stable-power-tempered-particle-model]] with
stability constant $B$, and fix $a,\beta>0$. In fixed reference length and
energy units, put $\Lambda_L=[0,L]^d$ and define, for $N\ge1$,
$$Z_{L,N}:=\frac{a^N}{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta U_N(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}\,d\lambda_d^{\otimes N},$$
where $\lambda_d$ is Lebesgue measure restricted to the Borel subsets of
$\mathbb R^d$, $\lambda_d^{\otimes N}$ is its $N$-fold product measure. The
integrand uses the ordinary real exponential when $U_N<+\infty$ and is defined
to be $0$ when $U_N=+\infty$. Also,
$\int_{\Lambda_L^N}f\,d\lambda_d^{\otimes N}$ abbreviates the nonnegative
integral of $f\mathbf1_{\Lambda_L^N}$ on the full product space, using
[[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]. Set $Z_{L,0}=1$.
Define $\Xi_L:=\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}Z_{L,N}$ as the nonnegative extended sum of
[[def-nonnegative-extended-series]]. For $L\ge1$ put
$Q:=a e^{\beta B}$. Choose any real $K>eQ+1$ and set
$$n_L:=\lfloor K L^d\rfloor+1.$$
which satisfies $K L^d<n_L\le K L^d+1$ by the integer-part lemma
[[lem-integer-part]]. Let
$\Xi_L^{\mathrm{cut}}:=\sum_{N=0}^{n_L}Z_{L,N}$. Then
$$1\le\Xi_L\le e^{Q L^d},\qquad \sum_{N>n_L}Z_{L,N}\le e^{-L^d},\qquad \Xi_L^{\mathrm{cut}}\ge(1-e^{-L^d})\Xi_L.$$

Let $d\ge1$ and let $\phi$ be power-tempered as in
[[def-tdmath-stable-power-tempered-particle-model]], with constants
$C,R,\epsilon>0$. Define
$$S_{d,\epsilon}:=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\bigl((2m+1)^d-(2m-1)^d\bigr)m^{-d-\epsilon},\qquad \|k\|_\infty:=\max_{1\le r\le d}|k_r| \quad(k\in\mathbb Z^d).$$
This nonnegative series, defined by [[def-nonnegative-extended-series]],
groups the lattice terms by shells $\|k\|_\infty=m$.
Then $S_{d,\epsilon}<\infty$. Let $\ell>0$, $g\ge R$, and let
$J\subset\mathbb Z^d$ be finite with $M=|J|$. For each $j\in J$, place at most
$n$ particles in the cube $C_j=(\ell+g)j+[0,\ell]^d$, where $n$ is a
nonnegative integer. The total absolute inter-cube energy satisfies
$$\sum_{\substack{j,j'\in J\;j<j'}}\;\sum_{q\in C_j}\sum_{q'\in C_{j'}}|\phi(q-q')|\le\frac C2 M n^2 S_{d,\epsilon}g^{-d-\epsilon}.$$
Here $j<j'$ means any fixed total ordering of the finite set $J$; each
unordered pair of cubes is counted once.

A measure space is a triple $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ where $\Sigma$ contains $\varnothing,X$ and is closed under complements and countable unions (a $\sigma$-algebra) of subsets of $X$ and $\mu:\Sigma\to[0,\infty]$ is countably additive with $\mu(\varnothing)=0$. A measurable function $f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]$ has measurable inverse images of Borel sets, where $[-\infty,\infty]$ has its order topology: finite open intervals and the endpoint neighborhoods $[-\infty,a)$ and $(a,\infty]$ form a basis. Its Borel sigma-algebra is generated by these open sets. A complex-valued function is measurable exactly when its finite real and imaginary parts are measurable, equivalently for the usual Borel structure of $\mathbb C$. Almost-everywhere assertions mean outside a measurable $\mu$-null set; completeness of $\mu$ is not assumed. Nonnegative extended addition uses $a+\infty=\infty+a=\infty$ for $a\in[0,\infty]$; positive scalars multiply $\infty$ to $\infty$, while $0\cdot\infty=0$. Signed expressions $\infty-\infty$ remain undefined and are not used in signed integrals. A nonnegative simple function has the form $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ with finitely many disjoint $A_j\in\Sigma$ and finite $c_j\ge0$. Define $c\mu(A)=+\infty$ if $c>0$ and $\mu(A)=+\infty$, define $0\cdot\infty:=0$, and define the finite sum of these extended nonnegative terms to be $+\infty$ if any term is $+\infty$ and otherwise the real finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]]. Then $\int s\,d\mu:=\sum_j c_j\mu(A_j)$; using canonical level sets $\{s=c\}$ makes this value representation-independent. For measurable $f\ge0$, define $\int f\,d\mu:=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: s\text{ is simple and }0\le s\le f\}$, using [[def-complete-ordered-field]] for a bounded set of finite values and setting the supremum to $+\infty$ when the values are unbounded or one is infinite. A real measurable $f$ is integrable when $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$, and then $\int f:=\int f^+-\int f^-$, where $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-:=\max(-f,0)$. Complex integrability and integration are defined by integrable real and imaginary parts.

Set $\alpha:=\frac12\bigl(1+d/(d+\epsilon)\bigr)$ and
$g_\ell:=\ell^\alpha$. Then $d/(d+\epsilon)<\alpha<1$ and
$\ell^d g_\ell^{-d-\epsilon}=\ell^{d-\alpha(d+\epsilon)}\to0$ while
$g_\ell/\ell\to0$. Fix a sufficiently large $\ell\ge1$ so that
$g_\ell\ge R$. For $L\ge\ell+g_\ell$, set
$m_L:=\lfloor L/(\ell+g_\ell)\rfloor$. Since $L/(\ell+g_\ell)\ge1$, [F10]
gives $m_L\ge1$ and
$m_L(\ell+g_\ell)\le L<(m_L+1)(\ell+g_\ell)$. Place $M_L=m_L^d$ cubes
$$C_j=(\ell+g_\ell)j+[0,\ell]^d,\qquad j\in\{0,\ldots,m_L-1\}^d.$$
They lie inside $[0,L]^d$ and have pairwise gaps at least $g_\ell$.

Fix occupancies $0\le N_j\le n_\ell$ with total $N=\sum_jN_j$. The
ordered configurations in the disjoint cubes with exactly these occupancies
are partitioned by assignments of the $N$ particle labels to cubes. The number
of assignments is $N!/(\prod_jN_j!)$: order all $N$ labels, then note that
each assignment occurs exactly $\prod_jN_j!$ times from within-cube reorderings.
Particle-permutation symmetry of $U_N$ and invariance of the finite product
measure (rectangle formula and uniqueness in [F6]) make the assignment
integrals equal.

Restrict the grand partition sum in $[0,L]^d$ to configurations with no
particles outside these cubes and at most $n_\ell$ particles in each cube,
where $n_\ell$ is the cutoff from [F2]. If two cubes have index difference
$k\ne0$, the coordinate gap in a coordinate attaining $\|k\|_\infty$ is at
least $\|k\|_\infty g_\ell$; [F3] therefore bounds the total absolute
inter-cube energy by
$$D_L\le\frac C2M_Ln_\ell^2S_{d,\epsilon}g_\ell^{-d-\epsilon}.$$
Thus $U_N=\sum_jU_{N_j}^{(j)}+U_{\mathrm{cross}}$ with
$U_{\mathrm{cross}}\le D_L$, and
$e^{-\beta U_N}\ge e^{-\beta D_L}\prod_j e^{-\beta U_{N_j}^{(j)}}$;
this remains true when an internal energy is $+\infty$, since both sides then
vanish.

On each assignment domain from step 2.1, the pointwise lower bound in
step 2.2 factors into nonnegative within-cube integrands. Repeated application
of [F5] and the rectangle formula in [F6] factors their integral into the
product of the translated one-cube integrals; [F7] identifies each with its
origin-centered value. Multiplying by $a^N/N!$ cancels the label count from
step 2.1, leaving $e^{-\beta D_L}\prod_j Z_{\ell,N_j}$. Summing over the
finitely many occupancy vectors and expanding the finite product of cutoff
sums from [F2] gives
$$\Xi_L\ge e^{-\beta D_L}(\Xi_\ell^{\mathrm{cut}})^{M_L}.$$

The integer-part bounds in step 1.1 give
$L/(\ell+g_\ell)-1<m_L\le L/(\ell+g_\ell)$, so
$m_L/L\to(\ell+g_\ell)^{-1}$ and $M_L/L^d\to(\ell+g_\ell)^{-d}$.
By [F2], $\Xi_\ell^{\mathrm{cut}}\ge(1-e^{-\ell^d})\Xi_\ell$, so
$\log\Xi_\ell^{\mathrm{cut}}\ge\ell^dp_\ell+\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})$.
Taking logarithms in step 3.1, dividing by $L^d$, and using step 2.2 gives
$$p_L\ge\frac{M_L}{L^d}\left(\ell^dp_\ell+\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})-\frac{\beta C}{2}n_\ell^2S_{d,\epsilon}g_\ell^{-d-\epsilon}\right).$$
Taking the lower limit and using the volume ratio above yields the same bound
with $M_L/L^d$ replaced by $(\ell+g_\ell)^{-d}$. The cutoff definition [F2]
and $\ell\ge1$ give
$n_\ell\le K\ell^d+1\le(K+1)\ell^d$. Factoring
$(\ell/(\ell+g_\ell))^d$ and using this estimate in the negative error term
therefore gives
$$\liminf_{L\to\infty}p_L\ge\left(\frac{\ell}{\ell+g_\ell}\right)^d\left[p_\ell+\ell^{-d}\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})-\frac{\beta C}{2}(K+1)^2S_{d,\epsilon}\ell^dg_\ell^{-d-\epsilon}\right].$$

As $\ell\to\infty$, the prefactor tends to $1$. Also
$e^{-\ell^d}\to0$, so continuity of $\log$ at $1$ gives
$\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})\to0$; since $\ell^{-d}\to0$, their product
$\ell^{-d}\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})$ tends to zero. The cross-energy error tends to
zero because $d-\alpha(d+\epsilon)<0$ by step 1.1. The replacement of the
prefactor times $p_\ell$ by $p_\ell$ has error at most
$Q\bigl[1-(\ell/(\ell+g_\ell))^d\bigr]\to0$ by [F2]. Thus for every
$\eta>0$ there is $T$ such that every $\ell\ge T$ makes the right side of
step 4.1 at least $p_\ell-\eta$.

Let $\overline p=\limsup_{\ell\to\infty}p_\ell$. By [A1], for every
$\eta>0$ and every $T\ge1$ there is an $\ell\ge T$ with
$p_\ell>\overline p-\eta$; otherwise the tail supremum from $T$ onward would
be at most $\overline p-\eta$, contradicting the infimum defining
$\overline p$. Choose $T$ large enough for step 5.1. Then
$\liminf_{L\to\infty}p_L\ge\overline p-2\eta$. Letting $\eta\downarrow0$
shows $\liminf p_L\ge\limsup p_L$.

For any $S,T\ge1$, choose $L\ge\max(S,T)$. Then
$\inf_{x\ge S}p_x\le p_L\le\sup_{x\ge T}p_x$. Taking the supremum over $S$
and then the infimum over $T$ proves
$\liminf p_L\le\limsup p_L$ by [A1]. Together with step 6.1, the two finite
tail bounds equal a number $p$. For every $\eta>0$, their definitions give
tail thresholds with $\inf_{L\ge T_-}p_L>p-\eta$ and
$\sup_{L\ge T_+}p_L<p+\eta$; hence $|p_L-p|<\eta$ for all sufficiently large
$L$. The limit is finite by [F2]. This proves existence for the specified
free-cube reduced grand pressure.

integrand uses the ordinary real exponential when $U_N<+\infty$ and is defined

$\int_{\Lambda_L^N}f\,d\lambda_d^{\otimes N}$ abbreviates the nonnegative

[[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]. Set $Z_{L,0}=1$.

$$n_L:=\lfloor K L^d\rfloor+1.$$
which satisfies $K L^d<n_L\le K L^d+1$ by the integer-part lemma

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $\phi$ be power-tempered as in
[[def-tdmath-stable-power-tempered-particle-model]], with constants
$C,R,\epsilon>0$. Define
$$S_{d,\epsilon}:=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\bigl((2m+1)^d-(2m-1)^d\bigr)m^{-d-\epsilon},\qquad \|k\|_\infty:=\max_{1\le r\le d}|k_r| \quad(k\in\mathbb Z^d).$$
This nonnegative series, defined by [[def-nonnegative-extended-series]],
groups the lattice terms by shells $\|k\|_\infty=m$.
Then $S_{d,\epsilon}<\infty$. Let $\ell>0$, $g\ge R$, and let
$J\subset\mathbb Z^d$ be finite with $M=|J|$. For each $j\in J$, place at most
$n$ particles in the cube $C_j=(\ell+g)j+[0,\ell]^d$, where $n$ is a
nonnegative integer. The total absolute inter-cube energy satisfies
$$\sum_{\substack{j,j'\in J\;j<j'}}\;\sum_{q\in C_j}\sum_{q'\in C_{j'}}|\phi(q-q')|\le\frac C2 M n^2 S_{d,\epsilon}g^{-d-\epsilon}.$$
Here $j<j'$ means any fixed total ordering of the finite set $J$; each
unordered pair of cubes is counted once.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement: A measure space is a triple $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ where $\Sigma$ contains $\varnothing,X$ and is closed under complements and countable unions (a $\sigma$-algebra) of subsets of $X$ and $\mu:\Sigma\to[0,\infty]$ is countably additive with $\mu(\varnothing)=0$. A measurable function $f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]$ has measurable inverse images of Borel sets, where the Borel sets of the extended real line are the sigma-algebra generated by its open sets. A nonnegative simple function has the form $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ with finitely many disjoint $A_j\in\Sigma$ and finite $c_j\ge0$. Define $c\mu(A)=+\infty$ if $c>0$ and $\mu(A)=+\infty$, define $0\cdot\infty:=0$, and define the finite sum of these extended nonnegative terms to be $+\infty$ if any term is $+\infty$ and otherwise the real finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]]. Then $\int s\,d\mu:=\sum_j c_j\mu(A_j)$; using canonical level sets $\{s=c\}$ makes this value representation-independent. For measurable $f\ge0$, define $\int f\,d\mu:=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: s\text{ is simple and }0\le s\le f\}$, using [[def-complete-ordered-field]] for a bounded set of finite values and setting the supremum to $+\infty$ when the values are unbounded or one is infinite. A real measurable $f$ is integrable when $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$, and then $\int f:=\int f^+-\int f^-$, where $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-:=\max(-f,0)$. Complex integrability and integration are defined by integrable real and imaginary parts.

With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$.

For a bounded set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $R>0$, define its two-sided boundary layer
$$\partial_R\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)\leq R\},$$
where distance is Euclidean distance and $|\cdot|$ denotes $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

For the unit cells $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$, there are constants $A>0$ and $B\geq0$ such that every finite configuration satisfies
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq A\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\omega)^2-BN(\omega).$$
Only finitely many summands are nonzero.
For free-boundary cubes define $\Xi_L(a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable.

derivations.claim:
Use the half-open unit-cell partition $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$ from [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]] and first take a finite union $\mathcal R$ of these cells. Let $\Pi_{\mathcal R}$ be the unnormalized positional sector measure whose $N$-point part is $z^N/N!$ times product Lebesgue measure, and let $\mu_{\mathcal R}$ have density $e^{-\beta H_{\mathrm{free}}}/\Xi_{\mathcal R}$ relative to $\Pi_{\mathcal R}$. By [L1] and Tonelli [F5],
$$E N_i^2=E N_i+E[N_i(N_i-1)] \leq \xi |C_i\cap\mathcal R|+\xi^2|C_i\cap\mathcal R|^2 \leq M:=\xi+\xi^2.$$
This gives a uniform second-moment bound for every unit cell in every such region.

For each $\Omega_k$, let $\mathcal R_k$ be the union of unit cells meeting $\Omega_k$. Then $\Xi_{\Omega_k}\leq\Xi_{\mathcal R_k}$ by domain monotonicity, and $|\mathcal R_k|/|\Omega_k|\to1$ by the van Hove boundary condition. Put $J_0=\lceil R_0+2\rceil$, where $R_0$ is the regular-tail cutoff in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and choose $M_0\geq\max\{2B,\psi(J_0-1)\}$. For $j\in\mathbb Z^d$, define $\kappa_j=M_0$ when $|j|_\infty<J_0$ and $\kappa_j=\psi(|j|_\infty-1)$ otherwise. If two particles occupy cells with offset $j$, their negative pair energy is bounded by $\kappa_j$: for near offsets, stability on a two-point configuration gives $\phi(x)\geq-2B$, and for far offsets the regularity envelope applies. Also $\sum_j\kappa_j<\infty$ by [F1]–[F2]. Partition the cells of $\mathcal R_k$ into boxes $B$ of $\ell$ unit cells per side and, for each occupied cell $i$, set $e_i=\sum_{j:\,B(j)\neq B(i)}\kappa_{i-j}$. The negative cross-box energy obeys $W^-\leq\sum_i e_iN_i^2$, by $N_iN_j\leq(N_i^2+N_j^2)/2$ and summation over ordered cross-box cell pairs. Step 1.1 gives $E W^-\leq M\sum_i e_i$, so Markov's inequality shows $W^-\leq2M\sum_i e_i$ with probability at least $1/2$ (with probability one if the sum vanishes). On this event $H_{\mathrm{total}}\geq H_{\mathrm{in}}-2M\sum_i e_i$, where $H_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the sum of within-box energies. Therefore
$$\Xi_{\mathcal R_k}/2\leq e^{2\beta M\sum_i e_i}\prod_B\Xi_{\mathcal R_k\cap B}.$$
Indeed, $\Xi_{\mathcal R_k}\mu_{\mathcal R_k}(E)=\int_Ee^{-\beta H_{\mathrm{total}}}d\Pi_{\mathcal R_k}$; bound this by $e^{2\beta M\sum_i e_i}\int_Ee^{-\beta H_{\mathrm{in}}}d\Pi_{\mathcal R_k}$, then factor the latter integral by boxes. Each unrestricted partial-box partition is at most the full $\ell$-cube partition. For one full box, put $E_\ell=\sum_{i\in B,j\notin B}\kappa_{i-j}$. For fixed $R$, cells within distance $R$ of the boundary contribute at most $O_R(\ell^{d-1})\sum_j\kappa_j$, while every other cell contributes at most $\ell^d\sum_{|j|_\infty>R}\kappa_j$. Thus $E_\ell/\ell^d\to0$, by first letting $\ell\to\infty$ and then $R\to\infty$. Consequently
$$\limsup_k|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log\Xi_{\Omega_k} \leq\ell^{-d}\bigl[\log\Xi_{\Lambda_\ell}+2\beta M E_\ell\bigr].$$
Let $\ell\to\infty$ and use [F4].

For the lower bound, put $q=ze^{\beta B}$ and choose $K>eq+1$. For integer core side $\ell\geq1$, let $n_\ell$ be an integer with $K\ell^d<n_\ell\leq K\ell^d+1$ and set $\Xi_\ell^{\rm cut}=\sum_{N=0}^{n_\ell}z^NZ(\Lambda_\ell,N;\beta)$. The stability tail estimate in the proof of [F4] gives $\Xi_\ell^{\rm cut}\geq(1-e^{-\ell^d})\Xi_{\Lambda_\ell}(z,\beta)$. Fix $g>2R_0$ and retain every complete $(\ell+g)$-tile whose core lies in $\Omega_k$. By [F2], the retained count $M_k$ divided by $|\Omega_k|$ tends $(\ell+g)^{-d}$. Each core has at most $(K+1)\ell^d$ particles. If two tile indices differ by maximum norm $m\geq1$, their core points are separated by at least $mg$; hence the positive cross energy per core is at most
$$C_d(K+1)^2\ell^{2d}\sum_{m\geq1}m^{d-1}\psi(mg)\leq C'_d(K+1)^2\ell^{2d}g^{-d}\eta(g).$$
Summing over cores, using the exact ordered-label assignment count to cancel the global $N!$, and discarding negative cross energy gives
$$\Xi_{\Omega_k}(z,\beta)\geq e^{-\beta D_{k,\ell,g}}(\Xi_\ell^{\rm cut})^{M_k},\qquad \frac{D_{k,\ell,g}}{|\Omega_k|}\leq C'_d(K+1)^2\left(\frac{\ell}{g}\right)^d\eta(g)+o_k(1).$$
First let $k\to\infty$. Then choose $g=g(\ell)$ from [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]] and let integer $\ell\to\infty$; $g/\ell\to0$, the packing fraction tends one, $(\ell/g)^d\eta(g)\to0$, and $\ell^{-d}\log(1-e^{-\ell^d})\to0$. The resulting liminf is at least the cube pressure [F4].

citations.quote:
Let $P$ be a set of primitive type labels. A formal type $\Gamma$ records a finitely supported amount function $\nu_\Gamma:P\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$, not identically zero. Primitive generators have their unit amount function. Positive scaling, separated product, and thermal-join constructors retain distinct formal tags and obey

$$\nu_{s\Gamma}=s\nu_\Gamma,\qquad \nu_{\Gamma\otimes\Gamma'}=\nu_\Gamma+\nu_{\Gamma'}\qquad(s>0).$$

Separated and joined types are distinct constructors even when their amount functions agree. Permutation, reassociation, and scaled-splitting conventions preserve the amount function. Define the positive **bookkeeping weight** $w_\Gamma:=\sum_{p\in P}\nu_\Gamma(p)$, a finite sum over support. Thus $w_{s\Gamma}=s w_\Gamma$ and every product or join has weight $w_\Gamma+w_{\Gamma'}$. The optional empty unit has zero amount function and weight zero; it is represented only by the empty compound, not as a simple chart. These are formal amounts, not masses in kilograms or an empirical conservation law. The functions and pointwise operations use [[def-function-space]]; their finite-support convention and finite sums are those of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] and [[lem-tdmath-compound-mass-well-defined]].

Let $I$ index the declared family of simple types $\Gamma_i$. For each simple type $\Gamma$ in that family, let $n_\Gamma\ge1$ and let $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^{n_\Gamma+1}$ be nonempty, open and convex, with coordinates $x=(u,v)$. The notation for a type and its chart is shared, but each state has a distinct raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$. Scaled charts are distinct tagged copies $s\Gamma=\{sx:x\in\Gamma\}$ with coordinate transport $x\mapsto sx$; transported raw tags remain distinct from the original raw tags. Let $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$ be the unit point mass from [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]]. The represented state is

$$\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x):=w_\Gamma e_{(\Gamma,x)},\qquad m(\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))=w_\Gamma.$$

Write $\mathsf{J}(x):=\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ when $x$ already carries its type tag. All state notation in this framework's compound comparisons, including a bare $x$, denotes $\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$; a raw unit point mass is always written $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$. A separated pair is addition of represented states, not a unit product tag. Nonnegative multiples are pointwise and zero terms are omitted. For an encoded compound $c$, its aggregate composition is the finite amount function

$$\nu(c):=\sum_{(\Gamma,x)\in\operatorname{supp}(c)}\frac{c(\Gamma,x)}{w_\Gamma}\nu_\Gamma;\qquad m(c)=\sum_{p\in P}\nu(c)(p).$$

Fix the formal interpretation $\Pi(c)$ as the finite separated preparation whose factor at each nonzero raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$ is the amount $c(\Gamma,x)/w_\Gamma$ of that typed state, using the declared coordinate scaling transport. The accessibility relation on coefficient maps is the pullback of the declared relation on these preparations. Merging or splitting repeated copies of the same preparation is reversible; permutation and reassociation preserve the preparation. Thus $\Pi(\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx))$ and $\Pi(s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))$ are the same declared scaled preparation and yield

$$\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx)\sim s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x),$$

although their raw point masses have different tags and are not equal. This reversible transport commutes with finite composition, nested type constructors, and scaled splitting. It is part of the precise formal scaling interpretation, not a deduction about physical accessibility from coordinate multiplication. A physical use must adopt the stated preparation maps and accessibility assumptions; fixed-composition models compare only preparations with the same $\nu$, while a declared channel model may additionally compare different compositions of equal $m$.

A comparison $A\prec B$ is defined only when $m(A)=m(B)$, as in the coefficient-map supplier. Write $A\sim B$ when both directions hold, and $A\prec\prec B$ when only the forward direction holds. On any fixed simple type, dividing every represented state by the same positive constant $w_\Gamma$ gives its unit-point-mass comparison. Positive scaling and its inverse preserve and reflect order; whenever the required CH and reference hypotheses hold, the unit-state entropy theorem applies after that normalization. If $S$ represents unit-point-mass comparisons, the entropy of a represented state is $w_\Gamma S(x)$ and the entropy of a finite sum $\sum_j t_j\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x_j)$ is $\sum_j t_j w_\Gamma S(x_j)$. No independent rescaling across different types is assumed without a calibrator.

The common relation satisfies A1–A6 on all equal-mass finite compounds: (A1) reflexivity; (A2) transitivity; (A3) if $A\prec B$, then $A+C\prec B+C$ for every compound $C$; (A4) if $A\prec B$, then $tA\prec tB$ for every $t>0$; (A5) $t\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ is equivalent to $s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)+(t-s)\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ for $t>0$ and $0<s<t$, with the reversible scaled-copy transport above; (A6) for equal-mass $A,B$, fixed positive equal-mass spectators $Z_0,Z_1$, and every sequence $\epsilon_n>0$ decreasing to zero, $A+\epsilon_n Z_0\prec B+\epsilon_n Z_1$ for all $n$ implies $A\prec B$. These are hypotheses, not conclusions. No comparison hypothesis is included here.

For each $i$ and $x\in\Gamma_i$, define the forward sector $A_x:=\{y\in\Gamma_i:\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)\prec\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)\}$. The simple-domain assumptions are: (A7) for $x,y\in\Gamma_i$ and $0<t<1$, the encoded compound $t\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+(1-t)\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)$ compares to $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(tx+(1-t)y)$; both have bookkeeping mass $w_{\Gamma_i}$, and convexity puts the recombined coordinate in the chart; (S1) each $x$ has a strict successor; (S2) $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane at $x$, expressible as $u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0$ with a finite-valued slope map $P_i:\Gamma_i\to\mathbb R^{n_i}$, and $P_i$ is locally Lipschitz; (S3) the boundary of $A_x$ relative to $\Gamma_i$ is arcwise connected. A supporting hyperplane means that $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets the plane at $x$. The affine hull is the smallest affine subspace containing a set; relative interior is interior in that affine hull. Closure and boundary are taken in the indicated affine hull or in $\Gamma_i$, as named; boundary is closure intersected with closure of the complement in that relative topology.

This definition imposes no physical interpretation, units, or empirical claim. A contact theorem that uses joins must separately assume that each join is a simple domain satisfying these same forward-sector hypotheses.

Let $I$ be a nonempty set of primitive simple-system labels containing a distinguished meter label $m$. Assume every finite separated product is explicitly represented by its finitely many tagged elementary factors; positive scaling and finite product are the only identifications. Suppose the join-closed family satisfies the hypotheses of [[thm-tdmath-conditional-contact-calibrator]], and fix a strict meter pair $z_0\prec\prec z_1$ in $\Gamma_m$. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Then one can choose, for every $i\in I$, an additive constant and positive scale for its same-type entropy so that

$$S\big((t_1i_1,x_1),\ldots,(t_ni_n,x_n)\big)=\sum_{\ell=1}^n t_\ell S_{i_\ell}(x_\ell)$$

is additive, extensive, and characterizes every same-composition comparison on every finite separated product. No conclusion is asserted for transitions that change composition.

Let $\mathcal G$ be a set of tagged system types closed under finite composition $T\times T'$ and positive scaling $tT$. Scaling is associative and acts componentwise on products: $s(tT)=(st)T$ and $t(T\times T')=(tT)\times(tT')$. Each type $T$ has a nonempty state set $X_T$ of finite tagged compounds, every state in $X_T$ is represented by the coefficient-map interpretation of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and has the fixed aggregate composition $\nu(a)=\nu_T$ of its declared type, using the amount-function interpretation in [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], and has total coefficient mass $m(T)=w_T\ge0$, and $\nu_{T\times T'}=\nu_T+\nu_{T'}$, $\nu_{tT}=t\nu_T$, with $m(T\times T')=m(T)+m(T')$ and $m(tT)=t\,m(T)$. Matching scalar masses alone do not identify aggregate composition. The entropy $\sigma_T:X_T\to\mathbb R$ is the finite additive extensive entropy from [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]]; in particular $\sigma_{tT}(ta)=t\sigma_T(a)$.

Include the formal empty unit type $1$, with $X_1=\{*\}$, $m(1)=0$, $\sigma_1(*)=0$, $T\times1=T$, and $t1=1$. A transition edge from type $T$ to type $T'$ is a pair $a\in X_T$, $b\in X_{T'}$ such that the underlying equal-mass compounds satisfy $a\prec b$ under [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Thus an edge can exist only when $m(T)=m(T')$. Its cost is the finite real number $\sigma_{T'}(b)-\sigma_T(a)$.

A decorated finite chain from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$ consists of a catalyst type $C\in\mathcal G$, an integer $N\ge1$, types $T_0=\Gamma\times C,T_1,\ldots,T_N=\Gamma'\times C$, and states $a_k\in X_{T_k}$, $b_{k+1}\in X_{T_{k+1}}$ with an edge $a_k\prec b_{k+1}$ for every $0\le k<N$. Its cost is the finite real sum

$$c=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\bigl(\sigma_{T_{k+1}}(b_{k+1})-\sigma_{T_k}(a_k)\bigr).$$

Define $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$ as the infimum of all such witness costs. Set $F=+\infty$ if there is no witness and $F=-\infty$ if the witness costs are unbounded below. The infimum is over real witness costs, so no subtraction of extended-real infima is used. Type permutations, reassociation, reversible identifications, and the identity $T\times1=T$ are part of the declared type structure. The cost identities and inequalities require a separate proof.

For the cost $F$ of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]], $F(\Gamma,\Gamma)=0$, $F$ is positively homogeneous, invariant under adding the same catalyst to both endpoints, and satisfies the triangle inequality whenever the extended-real sum on its right is defined. It is subadditive under composition whenever $F(\Gamma_1,\Gamma'_1)+F(\Gamma_2,\Gamma'_2)$ is defined. Every pair of actual forward and reverse decorated-chain witnesses has nonnegative total cost. A finite reverse witness therefore bounds all forward costs below; $F=-\infty$ can occur only when the reverse direction has no witness.

Under A1–A6 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], for compounds $A,B$ with $m(A)=m(B)$ and every finite spectator compound $C$, $A+C\prec B+C$ if and only if $A\prec B$. Consequently, for finite-support signed maps $u,v$ of equal total coefficient, define $u\preceq_s v$ by $(v-u)^-\prec(v-u)^+$. This relation is well-defined, agrees with $\prec$ on nonnegative maps, is invariant under adding a common signed map, is transitive, and is closed under addition of two comparisons. No comparison hypothesis is used.
In the complete ordered field $\mathbb R$, the sequence $\epsilon_n:=1/(n+1)$, $n\in\mathbb N$, is positive, strictly decreasing, and converges to zero.

derivations.claim: If $x\prec y$, the one-edge witness with an identity catalyst has cost $\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)$. Hence $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\le\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)$, which is the forward inequality, including the case $F=+\infty$ where no such transition can exist.

Conversely assume the displayed entropy inequality. It is impossible when $F=+\infty$. For each natural index $n\in\mathbb N$, use $\epsilon_n$ from [F5] and choose a decorated witness of real cost $c_n\le\Delta\sigma+h\epsilon_n$, where $\Delta\sigma=\sigma_{\Gamma'}(y)-\sigma_\Gamma(x)$ and $h=\sigma(z_1)-\sigma(z_0)>0$ is the entropy gap of a fixed strict meter pair from [F1]. Such witnesses exist from the definition of infimum, also if $F=-\infty$. Write their types as $T_0=\Gamma\times C,T_1,\ldots,T_N=\Gamma'\times C$, their edges as $a_k\prec b_{k+1}$, and their endpoints as $a_0=(\widetilde x,c_0)$, $b_N=(\widetilde y,d_0)$.

Put $\delta_n=\epsilon_n$. In one finite compound type form
$L_n=(x,b_N,b_1,\ldots,b_{N-1},\delta_n z_0),\qquad R_n=(a_0,y,a_1,\ldots,a_{N-1},\delta_n z_1).$
These have the same composition: both contain $\Gamma$, $\Gamma'$, the catalyst $C$, every intermediate type $T_1,\ldots,T_{N-1}$, and one scaled meter state, up to reassociation and permutation. Additivity of $\sigma$ and the definition of chain cost give
$\sigma(R_n)-\sigma(L_n)=\Delta\sigma-c_n+\delta_n h\ge0.$
Thus the same-composition entropy representation [F1] gives $L_n\prec R_n$.

Starting from $R_n$, use consistency on $a_0\prec b_1$ with $y,\delta_nz_1,a_1,\ldots,a_{N-1}$ as spectators. The result contains $b_1$ in place of $a_0$. Next use $a_1\prec b_2$ with $y,\delta_nz_1,b_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{N-1}$ as spectators, and continue in order. At stage $k$, the current compound contains $a_k$, the earlier outputs $b_1,\ldots,b_k$, all later inputs $a_{k+1},\ldots,a_{N-1}$, and the unchanged $y,\delta_nz_1$. After the last edge, transitivity gives $R_n\prec R'_n$, where $R'_n=(b_1,\ldots,b_N,y,\delta_nz_1)$. Compose this with $L_n\prec R_n$ from step 2.1. The compounds $L_n$ and $R'_n$ share the finite spectator $b_1+\cdots+b_N$; cancel it by [F4]. The result is $x+\delta_nz_0\prec y+\delta_nz_1$ for every $n$.

By [F5], $\delta_n\downarrow0$, stability in [A1] with bases $x,y$ and fixed positive spectators $z_0,z_1$ yields $x\prec y$. This proves the reverse implication without assuming that any infimum is attained.

Assume the calibrated entropy family of [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]], the cross-type accessibility axioms A1–A6 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], and the decorated cost $F$ of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. For every pair of types $\Gamma,\Gamma'$ and states $x\in X_\Gamma$, $y\in X_{\Gamma'}$,

$$x\prec y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sigma_\Gamma(x)+F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\le \sigma_{\Gamma'}(y).$$

The infimum defining $F$ need not be attained. If $F=+\infty$, the right side is false; if $F=-\infty$, the right side is true.

citations.quote: A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$.
The tail of the cell envelope $\psi(|j|_\infty-1)$ over all sufficiently large integer offsets is summable.

Then there are a nonnegative nondecreasing $h:\mathbb N_0\to[0,+\infty]$ with $h(0)=0$ and $h(N)/N^2\to+\infty$, and a constant $b<\infty$, such that
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}h(N_{C_i}(\omega))-bN(\omega).$$
The hard-core alternative permits $h(N)=+\infty$ above the finite packing capacity of a unit cell.
For free-boundary cubes define $\Xi_L(a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

derivations.claim: Put $S_n=\{i\in\mathbb Z^d:|i|_\infty\leq n\}$, $v_n=|S_n|=V_n$, $N_i(\omega)=|\omega\cap C_i|$, $T_n(\omega)=\sum_{i\in S_n}N_i(\omega)^2$, and $T_n^h(\omega)=\sum_{i\in S_n}h(N_i(\omega))$. Choose $m_0\geq\lceil R_0+1\rceil$ and $M_0\geq\max\{2B,\psi(m_0-1)\}$. Set $\gamma_m=M_0$ for integers $m<m_0$ and $\gamma_m=\psi(m-1)$ for $m\geq m_0$. Then $\gamma$ is nonincreasing, dominates the negative part at every cell offset, dominates $|\phi|$ at offsets $m\geq m_0$, and $\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}\gamma_{|j|_\infty}<\infty$ by [F1]–[F2]. Let $\Delta_m=\gamma_m-\gamma_{m+1}\geq0$ and $v_m=(2m+1)^d$. Since $\gamma_r=\sum_{m\geq r}\Delta_m$, Tonelli gives $\sum_m\Delta_m v_m=\sum_j\gamma_{|j|_\infty}<\infty$. Thus $\delta_k:=\frac12\sum_{m\geq k}\Delta_m v_m\to0$.

For an interior configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_n$ and any $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$, the long-offset cell sum satisfies
$$\sum_{i\in S_n,\ j\in\mathbb Z^d:\,|i-j|_\infty\geq k}\gamma_{|i-j|_\infty}N_i(\omega)N_j(\zeta)\leq\delta_k\bigl(T_n(\omega)+2^dtV_n\bigr).$$
Indeed, expand $\gamma_r=\sum_{m\geq r}\Delta_m$ and enlarge the offset set in the $m$th term to $j\in S_m+i$. With
$$S_{n,m}(\zeta)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z^d}N_j(\zeta)^2\,\#\{i\in S_n:j\in S_m+i\},$$
the inequality $ab\leq(a^2+b^2)/2$ bounds that term by $\frac12\Delta_m(v_mT_n+S_{n,m})$. The multiplicity is at most $\min(v_n,v_m)$ and vanishes unless $j\in S_{n+m}$, so $S_{n,m}\leq\min(v_n,v_m)t v_{n+m}\leq2^dtv_nv_m$. Summing proves the estimate.

Set $g(r)=r\sqrt{h(r)}$ for $r\in\mathbb N_0$ and $g^*(s)=\sup_{r\in\mathbb N_0}\{rs-g(r)\}$. Then $g(r)/r^2\to\infty$ and $g(r)/h(r)\to0$, so $g^*(s)/s^2\to0$: for each $a>0$, eventually $g(r)\geq r^2/(4a)$, and completing the square gives $g^*(s)\leq as^2+C_a$. Also $rs\leq g(r)+g^*(s)$. For a fixed $k\geq m_0$, every near cross pair has its inside cell in $S_n\setminus S_{n-k}$ and its exterior cell in $S_{n+k}\setminus S_n$; its negative energy is at most $M_0$. Counting the finitely many offsets of size below $k$, for every $a>0$ we obtain
$$W^-_{\rm near}\leq C_k\left(aT_n^h+C_a|S_n\setminus S_{n-k}|+atv_{n+k}+C_a|S_{n+k}\setminus S_n|\right).$$
Here $g(r)\leq ah(r)+C_a$ and $g^*(s)\leq as^2+C_a$ were used, with $\sum_{j\in S_{n+k}\setminus S_n}N_j(\zeta)^2\leq tv_{n+k}$. First choose $k$ large in step 1.2 so that its far negative-energy bound is at most $\epsilon(T_n^h+V_n)/2$. For this fixed $k$, both boundary-cell counts are $O_k(n^{d-1})$ and $v_{n+k}/v_n\to1$, so choosing $a$ small and then $n$ large makes the near bound at most $\epsilon(T_n^h+V_n)/2$. The far estimate uses $T_n\leq T_n^h+q^2V_n$ for a fixed $q$ with $h(r)\geq r^2$ when $r\geq q$. Consequently, for each $0<\epsilon<1$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
$$W_n(\omega,\zeta)\geq-\epsilon T_n^h(\omega)-\epsilon V_n$$
uniformly over $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$.

By [F3], $T_n^h\leq H_{n,\mathrm{free}}+bN$. For each $0<\epsilon<1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, step 1.3 therefore gives
$$\Xi_{n,\zeta}(z,\beta)\leq e^{\beta\epsilon V_n}\sum_{N\geq0}\frac{z^N}{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_N(\Lambda_n)}e^{-\beta H_{n,\mathrm{free}}+\beta\epsilon T_n^h}\,dq^N$$
and
$$\sum_{N\geq0}\frac{z^N}{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_N(\Lambda_n)}e^{-\beta H_{n,\mathrm{free}}+\beta\epsilon T_n^h}\,dq^N\leq\Xi(2n+1;ze^{\beta\epsilon b},\beta(1-\epsilon)).$$
The inequality is uniform over $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$.

For the lower bound, restrict interior particles to $\Lambda_{n-k}$, leaving the corridor empty. Choose $k\geq m_0$, so every interior-exterior cell offset is in the far tail. The two-sided estimate of step 1.2 gives
$$|W(\omega,\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n)|\leq\delta_k\bigl(T_{n-k}(\omega)+2^dtV_{n-k}\bigr).$$
With $T_{n-k}\leq T_{n-k}^h+q^2V_{n-k}$, choose $k$ large enough that the right side is at most $\epsilon(T_{n-k}^h+V_n)$. Since $T_{n-k}^h\leq H_{n-k,\mathrm{free}}+bN$, integration over the restricted positions yields
$$\Xi_{n,\zeta}(z,\beta)\geq e^{-\beta\epsilon V_n}\Xi(2(n-k)+1;ze^{-\beta\epsilon b},\beta(1+\epsilon))$$
uniformly over $\zeta$. For fixed $\epsilon$, the selected $k$ is fixed as $n\to\infty$, and the removed corridor volume fraction vanishes.

Divide the bounds in steps 2.1–2.2 by $V_n$ and let $n\to\infty$; [F4] supplies the perturbed free-cube pressure limits. These limits are finite convex functions of $(\beta,\log z)$ by Hölder's inequality [F5], since finite-volume log partition functions are convex and pointwise limits preserve convexity. A finite convex function is continuous on the open parameter domain $\beta>0$, $z>0$. Let $\epsilon\downarrow0$ in both uniform bounds. Their upper and lower limits coincide with $p(z,\beta)$ uniformly over $\Omega(t)$. For $t=0$, every exterior configuration in $\Omega(0)$ is empty, so the equality with the free-wall pressure is immediate.

Assume a stable regular pair potential with the genuine positive-core condition of [[lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core]]: a nonincreasing $\chi(r)>0$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ near zero and $\int_0^{r_0}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=\infty$. For fixed $z,\beta>0$, define the exterior class
$$\Omega(t)=\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\zeta)^2\leq t(2n+1)^d\text{ for every }n\}.$$
Then the free-wall grand pressure in $\Lambda_n=[-n-\tfrac12,n+\tfrac12)^d$, with the exterior pair energy against any $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$, converges to the free-cube pressure uniformly in $\zeta$. This statement is conditional on the genuine positive core; it does not infer that condition from superstability alone.

This statement is conditional on the genuine positive core; it does not infer that condition from superstability alone.

L1.title: D. Ruelle, Superstable Interactions in Classical Statistical Mechanics
L1.source_section: Section 6, printed pp.188–191 / PDF pp.18–21; complete relevant arguments and the Ruelle moment proof were read.
L1.source_statement: For a superstable lower-regular interaction, finite-volume and tempered-law estimates control near-boundary and far-tail contributions uniformly over the stated square-count class.

citations.quote:
With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$.

A van Hove sequence is a sequence of bounded Lebesgue measurable sets $(\Omega_k)_{k\geq1}$ with $0<|\Omega_k|<\infty$, $|\Omega_k|\to\infty$, and
$$\frac{|\partial_R\Omega_k|}{|\Omega_k|}\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{for every fixed }R>0.$$
The condition controls both inner and outer boundary neighborhoods.

For sequences $L_j\to\infty$ and integers $N_j\geq0$ with $N_j/L_j^d\to\rho$, define
$$b(\rho)=\sup\left\{\limsup_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta):\frac{N_j}{L_j^d}\to\rho\right\}.$$
Let $F$ be the concave envelope of $b$ on $[0,\infty)$, namely the supremum of $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i b(\rho_i)$ over finite lists with $\theta_i\geq0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\rho_i\geq0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i\rho_i=\rho$; the empty supremum is $-\infty$.

Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$.

Assume a superstable regular pair potential $\phi$ as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], with stability constant $B$, and the van Hove definition [[def-tdmath-van-hove-sequence]]. For a bounded Lebesgue-measurable $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$, define $\mathcal S_N(\Lambda)=\{(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\Lambda^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}$ and $H_N(q)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\phi(q_i-q_j)$. With $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, set
$$Z_\Lambda(N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_N(\Lambda)}e^{-\beta H_N(q)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_\Lambda(0;\beta)=1,\qquad \Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_\Lambda(N;\beta).$$
This is the labelled positional Lebesgue integral with indistinguishable-particle normalization and includes no exterior interaction. For $\Lambda=[0,L)^d$ it agrees with $Z(L,N;\beta)$ and $\Xi(L;z,\beta)$ from [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For every van Hove sequence $(\Omega_k)$ and fixed $z,\beta>0$, the free-wall grand pressure satisfies
$$\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac1{|\Omega_k|}\log\Xi_{\Omega_k}(z,\beta)=p(z,\beta),$$
where $p(z,\beta)$ is the free-cube limit from [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. The extra superstability hypothesis supplies the uniform cell-occupation bound used below; no arbitrary-shape theorem under stability alone is claimed.
Let $d\geq1$ and let $\phi$ be a regular potential with a nonnegative nonincreasing envelope $\psi:[R_0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, where $R_0<\infty$ and $\int_{R_0}^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr<\infty$.

derivations.claim: For any $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, $e^{\alpha N_k}Z(\Omega_k,N_k)\leq\Xi_{\Omega_k}(e^\alpha,\beta)$. Divide by volume, use [F5], and take the infimum over $\alpha$. The duality [F4] gives $\limsup |\Omega_k|^{-1}\log Z(\Omega_k,N_k)\leq F_\beta(\rho)$.

Choose $\delta>0$ so $\rho-\delta,\rho+\delta$ lie in the attainable interior. For large core side $\ell$, choose integers $n_-,n_+$ with $n_\pm/\ell^d\to\rho\pm\delta$. Put a central $\ell$-cube inside each $(\ell+g)$-cell, with $g=g(\ell)$ from [F6]. The effective densities $n_\pm/(\ell+g)^d$ still bracket $\rho$ when $\ell$ is large.

At fixed $\ell,g$, pack every complete $(\ell+g)$-cell contained in $\Omega_k$. Its count $M_k$ satisfies $M_k/|\Omega_k|\to(\ell+g)^{-d}$ by [F2]. Assign $n_+$ particles to $j_k$ cores and $n_-$ to the remaining cores, except one correction core with remainder $r_k$ chosen to make the total exactly $N_k$. Bracketing ensures $0\leq j_k<M_k$ for large $k$; Euclidean division gives $0\leq r_k<n_+-n_- \leq n_+$. Every correction integral $Z(\ell,r)$, $0\leq r\leq n_+$, is positive: delete particles from a positive-measure finite-energy set realizing $Z(\ell,n_+)>0$. There are finitely many such $r$, so the correction contributes $O_\ell(1)$ to the log weight.

Exact assignment of labels cancels the global $N_k!$, leaving the product of core canonical integrals. The core lattice shell estimate bounds cross-energy per volume by $C K^2(\ell/g)^d\eta(g)$, where $K\ell^d\geq n_+$. Let $k\to\infty$ first, then $\ell\to\infty$. The packing fraction tends one, the cross error tends zero, and the two rates tend $F_\beta(\rho-\delta)$ and $F_\beta(\rho+\delta)$. The bracketing proportions tend one half, so the lower rate is at least their average. Finally $\delta\downarrow0$; finite concavity makes $F_\beta$ continuous at the interior density. Combined with step 1.1 this proves the limit.

Assume superstability and regularity, let $(\Omega_k)$ be van Hove, and let $N_k/|\Omega_k|\to\rho$ for an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. For the free-wall exact-$N_k$ positional partition with $1/N_k!$ normalization,
$$|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log Z(\Omega_k,N_k;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the free-cube canonical rate of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Superstability is used for the arbitrary-shape pressure upper bound; no stability-only upper theorem is asserted.
